normalblockr: Gaussian Models with Latent Clustering of Variables

Source: R/normalblockr-package.R
normalblockr-package.Rd

Implements two families of Gaussian models with a latent clustering of the variables, for multivariate data whose variables co-vary, or respond to covariates, in groups. In the Normal-Block-Var model, the clusters structure the covariance through latent variables, and a network is inferred between the clusters rather than between the variables, which reduces its dimension and eases its interpretation (Tous and Chiquet (2026) doi:10.1016/j.csda.2026.108347 ). In the Normal-Block-Mean model, the variables of a cluster share the same regression profile, and a network between the variables can be inferred from their residual covariance. In both families, the clustering is either known or inferred, the network can be sparse (graphical lasso), and zero-inflated variants handle data with an excess of zeros. The parameters are estimated by expectation-maximization or variational expectation-maximization algorithms, accelerated by squared extrapolation, and a split and merge procedure improves the fits of a collection of models. The number of clusters, the sparsity of the network and the shape of the covariance are chosen with penalized criteria, cross-validation or stability selection.
